subject: Science
title: Look closely at rocks
objective_verbatim: Compare and group rocks by their appearance and simple properties.
reading_age_est: rough ARI grade 2.49 on 623 pupil-visible words; heuristic age guide 8.49 years, not a formal reading-age test
pupil_words: I am learning to look at rocks and sort them.
success_criteria: I can tell my sort rule.

vocab.definition: a solid thing from the ground
a small bit in a rock
things put together by a rule

retrieval.question: What are three ways to use less waste?
Which part helps you move with bones?

stages.pupil_text: Look at two safe rocks. Point to one you know.
stages.adult_text: Offer a safe kit choice and short first–then cue.

stages.pupil_text: Think back. Say, sign or point.
stages.adult_text: Ask three low-stakes prior questions; answers in note.
Pre-teach words; show the full model; ask the show-me check.

stages.pupil_text: Feel two rocks. Sort safe samples.
stages.adult_text: Hand over the missing step; offer F or H route. Reset once.

stages.pupil_text: Choose one answer. All of us show it.
stages.adult_text: Take all pupil responses at once; use decision rule and parallel hinge.

stages.pupil_text: Sort a safe rock. Show your rule.
stages.adult_text: Choose one adult for supported pupils, one for group; swap across the week.

stages.pupil_text: Show one sort. Hear one next step.
stages.adult_text: Give VF and one NS(+); invite one self-edit. Reset once.

stages.pupil_text: Show your rule to an adult.

worked_example.full: This rock feels rough. I put it with the rough rocks.
worked_example.faded: This rock feels smooth. I put it with the ____ rocks.
worked_example.removed_step: Name the group from an observed property.
worked_example.fade_next: Show two unlabelled samples; pupil names both groups.

cfu.question: Point to the sample that feels rough.
cfu.answer: The sample with the rough surface; depend on the real kit.

hinge.question: Two rocks look alike. How can you sort them?

options.text: Check one thing you can see or feel

options.diagnosis: Uses a label instead of checking.

options.text: Use only a photo of colour
options.diagnosis: Assumes one cue tells all properties.

hinge.decision_rule: About 3 in 4 or more right → move on; otherwise re-model This rock feels rough. I put it with the rough rocks. Ask the parallel hinge. No scores or answers saved.
hinge.parallel_hinge: Two rocks look different. Can they both fit the smooth group? Feel them. Yes, if both are smooth.

misconceptions.misconception: Rocks of the same colour must have the same feel.
misconceptions.correction: Use safe samples to check rough or smooth as well.

misconceptions.misconception: A rock can belong to only one group.
misconceptions.spot: Rejects the same rock from a new valid sort.
misconceptions.correction: Show one sample can be smooth and dark; name the rule each time.

we_do.support: Feel one safe rock. Point to rough or smooth.
we_do.stretch: Can one rock fit two groups? Name each rule.

tiers.F: Look at two rocks. Point to one change.
tiers.M: Sort two rocks by one thing you can check.
tiers.H: Sort the same rocks in two ways. Tell why.

stems.M: I put these in one group as they are ____.
stems.H: I can sort them by ____ and by ____.

tiers.go_deeper: Could one rock fit two groups? Show both rules.
tiers.early_finisher: Swap the rule. Which rocks move group, and why?

adaptations.cognition_learning: Give a three-step visual card for look closely at rocks; remove its last cue after a correct try.
adaptations.communication_interaction: Point to the real kit before a short spoken, signed or AAC response; wait for a turn.
adaptations.semh: Offer a private first–then cue and planned pause before the hinge; re-enter with one step.
adaptations.sensory_physical: Use a stable tray, large cards or an accessible input; no forced touch.
adaptations.eal: Rehearse a full M or H idea in any language before writing; keep the science challenge.

speaking_frames: I put these in one group as they are ____.
I can sort them by ____ and by ____.

ta_focus.i_do: Watch my first step. What do you see?
ta_focus.we_do: What step is missing? Show it with the kit.
ta_focus.independent: What can you do first on your own?

prompt_ladder: Point to the object or model.
Ask: What will you check next?
Model one step and give the next turn back.
Finish one example together, then let the pupil try.

F.a: The checked rough rock in the kit.
A solid thing from the ground.

M.q: How do you sort two rocks?
M.a: Check a feature such as rough or smooth.

H.q: Can one rock fit two groups?
H.a: Yes. It may be smooth and dark under two different rules.

H.q: What does our diagram leave out?
H.a: Real rocks must be checked by sight or safe touch.

diagrams.alt: Drawn rock samples show visible grains and a smooth face; a hand lens enlarges the grain view.
diagrams.caption: Look at grains with a hand lens. Compare with a smoother sample. Simplified; not to scale.

practical.prediction: Will the safe rocks feel the same?
kit: Two or more clean blunt rock samples
method: Place each rock in a group.
Check each group against the rule.
practical.risk: Check against the school risk assessment and CLEAPSS guidance. Check edges; no rock dust or tasting.
practical.pupil_risk: A rough edge may scratch skin.
practical.pupil_safety: Use clean blunt rocks. Keep them on the tray. Do not taste; wash hands after.

facts.claim: Different rocks can be grouped by appearance and simple physical properties.
A visible grain can be checked with a hand lens in a rock specimen.
Rough and smooth are observable material properties.
A rock can fit different valid groups when the rule changes.
Vocabulary term rock means a solid thing from the ground; example: I hold a safe rock.
Vocabulary term grain means a small bit in a rock; example: I see tiny grains.
Vocabulary term property means a thing you can check; example: This rock feels rough.
Vocabulary term group means things put together by a rule; example: These rocks are smooth.
Retrieval question from SoW C39: What are three ways to use less waste? Answer: Use less, use again, recycle.
Retrieval question from SoW C38: How do animals get food? Answer: From what they eat.
Retrieval question from SoW C35: Which part helps you move with bones? Answer: Muscles.
The “Grain rock” picture has drawn grains; the “Hand lens” can help inspect grains in a real specimen.
The “Smooth rock” picture contrasts surface texture; it does not assert a property of any particular specimen.
Pupil-facing practical risk statement: A rough edge may scratch skin.
facts.source: Local school risk assessment and CLEAPSS guidance; staff confirm exact kit
